newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian PM completes search for new government.
newsitem.headline: Estonian PM completes search for new government.

text.p: The prime minister of the Baltic state of Estonia on Sunday completed the formation of his new government, the seventh since the small nation quit the former Soviet Union five years ago.
The new government is set to be a minority administration, commanding just 41 seats in the 101-seat parliament.
The office of Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi said the premier had completed the formation of the government after President Lennart Meri approved five new ministers for the cabinet.
Vaehi was forced to find a new government after his previous junior coalition partner, the Reform Party, walked out.
"The vacancies left by the Reform Party have now been filled. The process of changing the government is now over," a spokeswoman for Vaehi told Reuters.
Vaehi had to find six new ministers for the cabinet and had last week named his foreign minister.
Five of the six are non-party ministers whom Vaehi hopes will find support amongst opposition parties.
The new foreign minister is Estonia's former U.S. ambassador, Toomas Ilves. Vaehi also filled the post of interior, education, social affairs, transport and economy minister.
